=========
 CORAM: HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE PURNENDU SINGH  ORAL ORDER 2 06-01-2026 Heard learned counsels appearing on behalf of the petitioners and the learned APP for the State.
2.
At the very outset, learned counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioners seeks to make correction in the cause title of the writ petition in course of the day.
3. Permission accorded.

4. The petitioners in paragraph no. 1 of the present writ petition has sought inter alia following relief(s), which is reproduced hereinafter:-
"(i) Issuance of a writ in the nature of mandamus or for any other appropriate writ(s),
order(s), direction(s) commanding the respondents to act in accordance with law relating to the construction of the National Highway No.333A starting from its junction with NH333 near Barbigha connecting Sheikhpur-Sikandra-Jamui, Jhajha- Banka, Panjwara, Bihar/Jhakhand Border in the State of Bihar to two/four lane with paved shoulder configuration programme in Mauza-Katoria, Anchal- Katoria, District-Banka in several khata and Kheshra of petitioners and other villagers has been mentioned in schedule of Bye-pass (Anchak-Katoria) and without Acquisition of the said land and without any proper notice to the petitioners (except one Rama @ Rambha Devi mother of Abhimanyu Prasad Singh.

Petitioner has received notice) and also direct the respondnets to make payment of compensation amount with interest for the admitted portion of the above said land of the petitioners, which is Patna High Court CWJC No.20509 of 2025(2) dt.06-01-2026 mentioned in schedule of By-pass Anchal-Katoria,
petitioners have no knowledge regarding any Award has been made regarding the acquisition of land.
(ii) Any other relief/reliefs to which the petitioner is found entitled to

. " 
5. That the brief facts of the case are that the respondents have constructed National Highway No.
333A starting from its junction with National Highway No. 333 near Barbigha connecting Sheikhpura - Sikandra - Jamui, Jhajha - Banka - Panjwara up to the Bihar-Jharkhand Border in the State of Bihar, by converting the same into two/four lane with paved shoulder configurations, and in Balkrishan Barnwal vs The State Of Bihar on 6 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99101460/

sentences.text:
3 the course of the said construction the land situated at Mauza - Katoria, Anchal - Katoria, District - Banka, which stands recorded in the name of the petitioners and in the name of his/her ancestors,
has been included, upon which on some portion of land the petitioners have constructed their pucca house and on some portion of land crops are growing till date, however the respondent authority,
while preparing the bye-pass schedule list of National Highway No. 333A, has shown the land upon which crops are growing as parti land and on some land has not shown the existing house and has wrongly written the same as parti land, thereby adversely affecting the lawful rights and interests of the petitioners.
Patna High Court CWJC No.20509 of 2025(2) dt.06-01-2026 6.

Learned counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioners submitted that in respect of the relief(s) as prayed for in the present writ petition, the petitioners have already filed a detailed representation before the District Land Acquisition Officer, Banka on 26.11.2025 but no action was taken by him and thereafter, the petitioners approached the District Magistrate-cum-Collector, Banka.
The District Land Acquisition Officer, Banka is sitting tight over their application leading to filing of the present writ petition.

7. This Court without going into the merits of the case directs the District Magistrate, Banka to exercise his jurisdiction and see that why the District Land Acquisition Officer, Banka has not taken any action even though from the information contained in the writ petition it appears that the amount of compensation has already been notified and the petitioners have been deprived of the due amount of compensation in lieu of their land acquired for the purpose of National Highway 333A starting from its junction.

8. The District Magistrate, Banka, if finds that the petitioner is entitled for the relief(s) as prayed for in the present writ petition, must ensure to make payment of the amount of compensation well within a period of one month from the date Patna High Court CWJC No.20509 of 2025(2)
dt.06-01-2026 of communication of this order.
9. With the above observation/direction, the present writ petition stands disposed of.
10. It is made clear that the above order has been passed in presence of Ms. Ankita Kumari, learned counsel, who has tendered her appearance on behalf of NHAI.

(Purnendu Singh, J) chn/-
